text:
maria: Heads up — canary pool in us-west-2 started flapping right after the container rebuild wave with the CUDA12 runtime. NCCL collectives are hanging during all-reduce, and we see lots of TCP retransmits on the host.
kevin: Which instance family? g5/g4? I saw similar on a mixed g4dn/g5a pool earlier.
sophia: deploy-bot pushed runtime: redwood/runtime:cuda12-2026-03-17 at 11:03 UTC to canaries :package:
deploy-bot: image pushed redwood/runtime:cuda12-2026-03-17
maria: Repro steps (from a failing canary):
```
kubectl exec -it nccl-test -- bash
python3 run_allreduce.py --size 256MB --rank 0
# process hangs after the init phase
```
And logs have repeating lines like:
```
NCCL INFO Net: > tcp://10.0.3.45:5678
NCCL WARN NET/Socket : recv returned 104 (Connection reset by peer)
NCCL WARN NET/Socket : send returned -1 (Resource temporarily unavailable)
NCCL ERROR UNRECOVERABLE: unexpected network error
```
yusuf: nvidia-smi on affected nodes:
```
NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12 Driver Version: 525.85.12 CUDA Version: 12.0
+-------------------------------+
| Processes:  GPU   PID   Type   |
+-------------------------------+
```
maria: Toolkit binaries in the image were built against newer libstdc++ (GLIBCXX_3.4.30) but host driver/lib exposes older symbols — ldd shows mismatches. Running `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so` on a canary prints unresolved references.
kevin: We rebuilt the image to rely on distro-provided libstdc++ to shrink image size; looks like that removed the ABI that NCCL (prebuilt) expects. Also saw the container runtime dropping the bundled nv_peer_memory kernel module load.
sophia: Also spotted MTU changes — CNI apparently reverted jumbo frames to 1500 when new nodes came up. NCCL prefers RDMA/EN interface with MTU 9000; falling back to TCP over 1500 can cause stalls for large collective traffic.
maria: Quick mitigation proposals:
- revert canary nodes to previous image tag (cuda11) for now
- pin driver on host to 535.x (we're on 525) or rebuild NCCL against 525 to match
- force MTU 9000 on ENIs for the canary SGs
- temporarily disable the image rollout
kevin: Rollback command ready:
```
kubectl -n infra set image ds/nccl-canary runtime=redwood/runtime:cuda11-2026-02-28
```
sophia: I'll flip the MTU config in the CNI daemonset for the canary subnet and restart agents. If that fixes collectives, we can rule out the network path.
yusuf: Ops/Cost note: holding a significant portion of fleet on cuda11 will increase our short-term committed spend and complicate capacity planning for Dedicated customers. We need a timeline for a proper rebuilt image (relink NCCL with system libs or rebuild NCCL from source against new toolchain).
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-142 created for us-west-2 canary NCCL hangs (priority P2)
maria: Action items: 1) sophia to set MTU and confirm, 2) kevin to publish a hotfix image (link NCCL->system lib or include libstdc++), 3) yusuf to model cost delta for 48h rollback window. I'll pause the global CUDA12 rollout until we get green in canaries.
kevin: Will push hotfix image by EOD and report back.
sophia: MTU change applied to canary subnet, restarting agents now. Will post nccl-test logs in 10m.
maria: Thanks — please @here if you see an uptick in repeaters or kernel oops. We'll decide on driver pin vs image rebuild after hotfix verification. :handshake:
